shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar carved in low relief
top register of three repeated arch- or U-shaped enclosures containing paired elements
horizontal band/register divider running the full width
band of short vertical strokes (fringe or comb-like hatching)
rounded oval/circular bosses or disc motifs
small figural motifs arranged in a lower register
justification: The most specific correspondence is the shared compositional scheme: a row of three repeated arch/U-shaped enclosures across the top, closed off by a horizontal band with a fringe of short vertical strokes, above a register of smaller rounded or figural motifs, all executed in shallow, flat-planed relief on tan stone. The biggest difference is that A's lower zone is dominated by large abstract ovals and a concentric disc on what reads as a body-like, tapering monolith, whereas B's lower register carries recognisable profile creatures on a flat rectangular slab, and A's surface is far more weathered and rounded than B's crisp edges.
